additions.description: The DELETE /todos/{id} endpoint returns a JSON message {"message": "Todo deleted"} on success.
additions.reasoning: The specification requires that DELETE /todos/{id} returns status 200 OK on success but does not specify any response body. The code returns a JSON message which is not required by the specification.

additions.description: The POST /users/register endpoint returns the created user object with id and email.
additions.reasoning: The specification states to verify response status 200 OK on registration but does not require returning the user object. Returning the user object is an addition.

additions.description: The POST /users/login endpoint returns a TokenResponse model with access_token and token_type fields.
additions.reasoning: The specification requires returning an access token on login but does not specify the response structure or token_type field. Returning token_type is an addition.

omissions.description: POST /todos does not validate that the title field is present and non-empty; no 400 Bad Request is returned if title is missing or empty.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that POST /todos with empty or missing title returns 400 Bad Request with a validation error indicating 'The Title field is required.' The code does not perform this validation explicitly.

omissions.description: PUT /todos/{id} does not check that the id in the request body matches the id in the URL path; no 400 Bad Request is returned if they differ.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that if the id in the PUT request body differs from the URL id, the response is 400 Bad Request. The code ignores the id field in the body and does not validate it.

omissions.description: GET /todos and other endpoints do not return 401 Unauthorized if Authorization header or token is missing.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that calling GET /todos without Authorization header returns 401 Unauthorized. The code uses HTTPBearer with auto_error=False and raises 401 if credentials are None, so this is implemented correctly. No omission here.

omissions.description: POST /users/register does not validate that the email and password fields are present and valid; no explicit validation errors are returned.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires registration with valid email and password but does not specify validation errors. The code relies on Pydantic for EmailStr and password presence, so this is implicitly handled. No omission here.

omissions.description: PUT /todos/{id} does not verify ownership before updating; it only checks if the todo exists for the current user, but does not handle the case where the todo exists but belongs to another user.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that if a user tries to update a todo they do not own, the response is 404 Not Found. The code queries with Todo.id == id and Todo.user_id == current_user.id, so it returns 404 if not found or not owned. This is implemented correctly. No omission here.

omissions.description: DELETE /todos/{id} does not verify ownership before deleting; it only deletes if the todo belongs to the current user, otherwise returns 404 Not Found.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that deleting a todo not owned by the user returns 404 Not Found. The code queries with Todo.id == id and Todo.user_id == current_user.id, so it returns 404 if not found or not owned. This is implemented correctly. No omission here.
